tier1.text: Each temporal bone helps form the brain case, the part of the skull that surrounds and protects the brain. Each temporal bone forms the lower part of one side of the skull. Inside each temporal bone is the inner ear, which contains the sense organs for hearing and balance. The mandible, or lower jaw, joins each temporal bone at a joint that lets the mouth open and close.

quotes.quote: The brain case surrounds and protects the brain, which occupies the cranial cavity inside the skull. It consists of the rounded calvaria and a complex base. The brain case is formed by eight bones, the paired parietal and temporal bones
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: brain case: portion of the skull that contains and protects the brain, consisting of the eight bones that form the cranial base and rounded upper skull
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The condyle of the mandible articulates (joins) with the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone. Together these articulations form the temporomandibular joint, which allows for opening and closing of the mouth
